title: Pavel Durov at DLD12: why altruistic, information-rich web services outlast communication fads
summary: Durov, in his first public appearance, shares VK's scale and a framework for judging how durable a web project is. Services that accumulate useful information and avoid greedy monetization (Wikipedia) last longer than pure communication tools, which are prone to fashion. The rest of the session is Jimmy Wales on SOPA, not Durov's content.

principles.text: Web projects that accumulate widely useful, searchable information are more robust and longer-lived than pure communication tools.
principles.quote: the projects on the left tend to be more robust and more longterm because the ones on the right are often prone to Fashion

principles.text: Services that stockpile information grow more important and useful over time as the stored knowledge grows.
principles.quote: the services of the left they grow more and more important and more and more useful uh as times go by and they accumulate more and more widely uh useful and searchable information

principles.text: Greedy monetization drives users away; early social networks that overcharged or over-advertised declined.
principles.quote: classmates.com at the top one of the first social networks but it was so greedy that judged its users for uh sending private messages and uh eventually uh it came to decline

principles.text: Platforms built on user-generated content must make users feel cared for, not used, or loyalty erodes.
principles.quote: users must not feel uh offended that must not feel used by the service uh this might they must feel that uh this the service cares about them

principles.text: Communication tools are prone to fashion because users can switch to another one tomorrow, so lasting value needs stored information.
principles.quote: you can use one instant messaging today one instant messaging system today and then switch to some other inant messaging tomorrow

principles.text: Being too hard on advertising makes users less loyal and contributed to the decline of a major social network.
principles.quote: they were too hard on adver advertisements and uh uh users become less loyal to them
